steps.html:
A beetle in the Namib desert collects its own drinking water overnight. A twenty-four-year-old student in Melbourne noticed, and turned it into a machine that waters crops without rain.

  • Read two profiles of award-winning designs
  • Use the passive in all its main forms
  • Describe how something works
  • Write a description of an invention

steps.title: The machine that was designed by a beetle
steps.html:
Reading 1 · 147 words

Australia's worst drought in a century was still being reported nightly when Edward Linacre, a design student in Melbourne, began looking for a way of watering crops without rain.

The answer was found in the Namib desert, where almost no rain falls at all. The Namib beetle survives there by collecting moisture on its own back: the air cools against the shell overnight and water condenses on it, drop by drop.

The Airdrop copies that. Air is drawn down through underground pipes, where it is cooled by the soil until the moisture it carries condenses. The water is then delivered straight to the roots. Nothing is wasted and no electricity is generated on site; a small turbine does the work.

The design was shortlisted for the James Dyson Award and then won it. Linacre was twenty-four. The judges said it was the most functional entry they had been given.

steps.title: What problem was the Airdrop designed to solve?
options: How to store water in a tank without it evaporating.
How to water crops in a place where it does not rain.
How to generate electricity on a farm.
steps.answer: How to water crops in a place where it does not rain.
steps.why: Linacre 'started looking for a way of watering crops without rain'.

steps.title: Three more that were shortlisted
steps.html:
Reading 2 · 146 words

Twenty engineers and designers are shortlisted for the award each year, and the entries that are remembered are rarely the most complicated.

Suncayr was invented by a group of Canadian students. It is a pen. You draw on your skin with it before applying sunscreen, and the mark changes colour when the protection has stopped working. Nothing is measured and nothing is charged.

The Xarius is a small wind turbine that can be folded into a bag and attached to almost anything. It generates enough power to recharge a phone, which sounds unremarkable until you consider where it is meant to be used.

The Sono is stranger. It is placed on a window, and the noise coming through the glass is cancelled — except for the frequencies you have chosen to keep. The middle is twisted to control which sounds are let in. It has not been produced commercially.

You draw on your skin with it, and the mark changes colour when the protection stops working.
It charges a device using sunlight.
steps.answer: You draw on your skin with it, and the mark changes colour when the protection stops working.
steps.why: 'Nothing is measured and nothing is charged.'

steps.prompt: Why is that exception the interesting part of the design?
options: Because a selective filter is cheaper to build than a total one.
Because it treats noise as something to be selected rather than removed, which is a different problem from silence.
Because most users end up keeping every frequency in the end.
steps.answer: Because it treats noise as something to be selected rather than removed, which is a different problem from silence.
steps.why: A device that removed everything would be simpler and worse. The exception is what turns a noise blocker into a filter.

steps.title: When the doer is not the point
steps.html:
All the forms, in one place, and the reason for using any of them.

The passive is be in the right tense + the past participle. The object of the active sentence becomes the subject: They shortlisted the design → The design was shortlisted.

Use it when the doer is unknown, obvious, unimportant, or when you want to keep the focus on the thing rather than the person. Descriptions of how something works are almost entirely passive, because the machine matters and the operator does not: Air is drawn down through pipes, where it is cooled by the soil.

If the doer does matter, add it with by: Suncayr was invented by a group of Canadian students. Most passive sentences have no by phrase at all.

Only verbs that take an object can be made passive. Happen, arrive, exist, rain cannot: an accident was happened.

Watch two things at B2. The be carries the tense, not the participle: is drawn / was drawn / has been drawn / will be drawn / is being drawn / had been drawn. And after a modal, use be + participle: it can be folded, not can folded.

steps.title: Example bank.
steps.html:
Twelve sentences from the two texts.

The answer was found in the Namib desert.
Past simple passive; the finder is not the point.

Australia's drought was still being reported nightly.
Past continuous passive.

Air is drawn down through a network of pipes.
Present simple passive — how it works.

It is cooled by the surrounding soil.
With by, because the soil does the cooling.

The water is then delivered straight to the roots.
Sequence of passives, no agent named.

Nothing is wasted.
Passive with a negative subject.

No electricity is generated on site.
Same pattern.

The design was shortlisted and then won it.
Passive, then active. Both are fine in one sentence.

the most functional entry they had been given
Past perfect passive.

Suncayr was invented by Canadian students.
The agent matters here, so it is named.

It can be folded into a bag.
Modal + be + participle.

It has not been produced commercially.
Present perfect passive, negative.

steps.title: Turning a description into the passive
steps.html:
1. The active version: The machine draws air down through pipes. The soil cools it. The pipes deliver the water to the roots. Three sentences, all about the machine doing things.
  2. In a description of how something works, the reader wants the process, not the machine as an actor. Make the object the subject: Air is drawn down through pipes.
  3. Keep the agent only where it adds information. The soil does: It is cooled by the surrounding soil. The pipes does not: The water is then delivered to the roots.
  4. Check the tense sits on be, not on the participle: is drawn, not is draw; was drawn, not was drew.
  5. Result: Air is drawn down through pipes, where it is cooled by the surrounding soil. The water is then delivered to the roots.

options.label: Something in your home you could not do without
Something you would like somebody to invent

steps.title: Write your description.
steps.sub: 140–170 words. Explain what problem it solves and how it works. Use at least six passive forms, in at least three different tenses.
steps.placeholder: The problem it was designed to solve is …
steps.html:
• Open with the problem the invention was designed to solve.
  • Describe how it works, mostly in the present passive.
  • Give one fact about who invented it and when, in the past passive.
  • Say what has happened to it since, in the present perfect passive.

Useful language

  • It was invented in … by …
  • The problem it was designed to solve is …
  • Air / water / heat is drawn / cooled / collected …
  • Nothing is wasted, and no … is needed.
  • It can be folded / attached / carried …
  • It has not been produced commercially.
steps.modelHtml:
The thermos flask

The problem it was designed to solve is very old: how to keep something hot without heat being added to it. Most of a hot drink's heat is lost through the walls of whatever it is kept in.

The flask is built as two containers, one inside the other, and the air between them is removed. Because heat cannot be carried across a vacuum, almost nothing is lost that way. The inner surfaces are then silvered, so that the heat that would otherwise be radiated is reflected back in.

It was invented in 1892 by James Dewar, who was studying gases at very low temperatures and needed somewhere to keep them. It was never patented by him. Within twenty years it was being sold to anybody who wanted to take soup to work, and it has been made in the same way ever since.
